rulings.challenge_claim: the row's ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Prov.21.29 mislabels the second variant pair as 'the pronoun'; the affected word is the noun 'way' carrying a pronominal suffix (ketiv plural / qere singular), not a free-standing pronoun
rulings.grounds: Byte tier (collate.py GREEN): oshb:Prov.21.29 closing clause reads יכין יָבִ֬ין דרכיו דַּרְכּֽוֹ (inline-ketiv pattern: unpointed ketiv token precedes its pointed qere, per the TOOLKIT inline-ketiv hazard). pmarks_Prov.json kq confirms exactly 2 notes at Prov.21.29, matching the row's count. Pair 1 (יכין/יָבִ֬ין) is a finite verb, correctly labeled 'the verb' by the row. Pair 2 (דרכיו ketiv, plural consonants 'his ways' / דַּרְכּֽוֹ qere, pointed singular 'his way') is the noun derekh ('way') bearing a 3ms pronominal suffix; the K/Q variance is grammatical NUMBER on the same noun (plural ketiv vs singular qere), not a substitution of a free-standing pronoun. The row's rationale phrase 'the verb and pronoun of that closing clause' therefore mislabels pair 2's part of speech. OL's correction is byte-accurate; the K/Q note COUNT of 2 stays correct either way, so the isolation/support verdict on the row is unaffected.
rulings.remedy: In P09-059's rationale, replace 'the verb and pronoun of that closing clause' with a part-of-speech-accurate phrase (e.g. 'the verb and the suffixed noun for way of that closing clause'). Cure test: the corrected phrase must not use 'pronoun' as the label for דרכיו/דַּרְכּֽוֹ; re-verify by re-collating oshb:Prov.21.29 at byte tier and re-checking pmarks kq Prov.21.29=2 against the corrected wording.

rulings.challenge_claim: device_notes overstates the internal grammar of 22:17-21 as 'one periodic sentence' when the bytes show two distinct governing clauses; and the boundary_evidence_refs citation of web:Prov.23.1-Prov.23.1 is never argued in the prose
rulings.grounds: Grammar sub-claim UPHELD as stated: byte-level clause analysis confirms at least three distinct governing/finite verbs across vv.17-20 rather than one continuous period -- the imperative pair at Prov.22.17 (opening the address), a first-person perfect main verb הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ ('I have made known to you') at Prov.22.19 closing its own clause, and a fresh interrogative-perfect main verb כָתַ֣בְתִּי ('have I not written') opening Prov.22.20. Verse 21's two purpose infinitives לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ and לְהָשִׁ֥יב attach most naturally to the nearest preceding finite verb, כָתַ֣בְתִּי at v.20 ('have I not written... in order to make you know... to return...'), not to v.17's imperative chain. LF's redescription (vv.17-19 imperative+purpose; vv.20-21 rhetorical-question+purpose, unified by address function) is the better-grounded reading of these same bytes than device_notes' 'one periodic sentence.' Citation sub-claim REFINED: the rationale itself never mentions Prov.23.1. But device_notes does name-check '23:1' once, as a passing texture remark ('...distinct from the sentence-literature run that follows in 23:1 onward'), not as a substantiated boundary argument -- no quote or clause analysis of Prov.23.1 ties it to the boundary_evidence_refs entry. So 'never argued in the prose' overstates the defect slightly (the ref is not wholly unmentioned); the corrected finding is that web:Prov.23.1-Prov.23.1 is cited in boundary_evidence_refs but only name-checked as texture in device_notes, never substantively argued as boundary evidence anywhere in the row. Independently reverified and NOT disturbed by either sub-claim: the row's span and closing boundary remain sound. Skeleton comparison (consonantal_index.json) shows oshb:Prov.22.16 and oshb:Prov.22.17 share zero content tokens (clean C2|C3 collection seam per book_strategy/Prov.md section 5); the divrei-hakhamim phrase דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים at Prov.22.17 sits at words 4-5 of an 8-word verse (mid-verse, not header), matching the book-wide pattern at oshb:Prov.1.6 where the same phrase דִּבְרֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים also sits at words 4-5 of a 6-word verse; prov_device_inventory.json divrei_hakhamim_anywhere confirms these are the only 2 book-wide sites (count=2). pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE at Prov.22.21 exactly as reported by the row and both primaries.
rulings.remedy: (1) Re-cut device_notes to describe vv.17-21 accurately: address-function-unified but grammatically two governing movements (imperative address vv.17-18 with its motive at v.18; first-person disclosure vv.19-21 built on הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ/כָתַ֣בְתִּי with v.21's infinitives attaching to v.20's verb), replacing 'one periodic sentence.' Cure test: re-parse oshb:Prov.22.17-Prov.22.21 clause-by-clause and confirm the revised device_notes correctly attaches v.21's infinitives to their antecedent verb (the test that killed the original). (2) Either delete the web:Prov.23.1-Prov.23.1 entry from boundary_evidence_refs, or add one sentence to the rationale that actually argues it (e.g., noting 23:1 opens an unrelated court/dining scenario sharing no skeleton token with 22:17-22:21, corroborating the close at the 22:21 petuchah). Cure test: every boundary_evidence_refs entry must have a corresponding argued sentence in the rationale, not just a device_notes mention.

rulings.challenge_claim: unit_type single_proverb misclassifies Prov.22.28 (a C3 span); book_strategy/Prov.md section 6 names admonition_unit as C3's operative category and grants single_proverb explicitly only to C4, with no equivalent grant for C3
rulings.grounds: book_strategy/Prov.md section 6 (worktree, read-only) states verbatim: 'C3: admonition_unit (~2-4 vv imperative units; 22:17-21 is the prologue). C4: admonition_unit/single_proverb per bytes.' C4's grant explicitly lists two disjunctive unit_types; C3's grant names only admonition_unit, with no '/single_proverb' disjunct. P10-005's parent_collection field reads 'C3 Prov.22.17-Prov.24.22', and Prov.22.28 falls inside C3's span (section 5: C3 = 22:17-24:22), so C4's disjunctive grant does not apply, nor does C2/C5's separate 'SINGLE_PROVERB DEFAULT' rule (P10-005 is not in C2 or C5) -- confirming the cluster's C2|C3 seam-awareness duty: rows P09-059/065/072 (C2, 21:29/22:4/22:11) correctly use C2's single_proverb default, while P10-001..005 (C3) must use C3's admonition_unit grant, not C2's rule. Byte content of oshb:Prov.22.28 (opening אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל, 'do not move the ancient boundary') is a bare negative-imperative maxim, the same imperative-opening pattern as the row's own neighboring admonition_unit rows in this cluster (Prov.22.22, Prov.22.24, Prov.22.26, all also opening with a negative particle plus imperative). Section 6's C3 definition ('admonition_unit... imperative units') states no explicit minimum span nor requires a separate motive clause as a defining trait; the row's own point -- that 22:28 lacks a motive clause unlike its 2-verse neighbors -- argues for a one-verse structural sub-variety of admonition_unit, not a different controlled-vocabulary category. The single_proverb label is therefore a controlled-vocabulary violation of the owner ruling for this collection. Span itself unaffected: independently reverified that oshb:Prov.22.28's opening 3 words (אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל) match oshb:Prov.23.10's opening 3 words byte-for-byte, confirming the row's non-adjacent-recurrence claim; this does not change the C3 unit_type requirement.
rulings.remedy: Change unit_type from single_proverb to admonition_unit for Prov.22.28-Prov.22.28; re-cut the rationale/device_notes to justify admonition_unit status on its own terms (bare one-verse imperative maxim, no motive clause, distinct from the two-verse imperative+motive admonition_unit rows around it, still satisfying C3's imperative-unit test) rather than arguing toward single_proverb. Cure test: unit_type for every row whose parent_collection is C3 must be a value section 6 grants to C3 (admonition_unit) unless the owner amends section 6, verified against the book_strategy/Prov.md section 6 text. PROPOSAL ONLY (requires explicit boss adoption, not applied here): 22:28's one-verse atomicity (no motive clause, plus the byte-confirmed non-adjacent verbatim recurrence of its opening at Prov.23.10) is a structural argument the owner could consider for extending C4's 'admonition_unit/single_proverb per bytes' grant to comparable atomic C3 verses.
